tldr: The entire public clique-size spectrum evaluates isolated direct-effect precision when memberships are hidden. For deterministic real local tables with only the two target exposures bounded, the hidden minimax risk is equivalent to \(q(s)\), while supplied memberships give risk equivalent to \(S_2(s)\). A polynomial-bit computation selects a total graph-free Bernoulli design and an own-treatment score applied to clipped observations. The unrestricted lower comparison retains every label and seed and tests the realized fixed-table target. Both games are consistent exactly when the largest cell weight vanishes; the maximal membership price is \(\Theta(n^{1/3})\). Matching and equal-size endpoints are occupied antecedents; the new result is the uniform heterogeneous surface.
